name: Confirmed 18-Ritual Foundation Library
description: A data-driven, wellness-oriented ritual catalog. Optional symbolic supports are always offered as choices, not requirements.

rituals.intendedResult: Begin the day with grounded contact and one realistic intention.

steps.title: Feel the contact
steps.instruction: Notice where your feet meet the floor or your shoes. Let the support beneath you be enough for this moment.

steps.title: Allow one easy breath
steps.instruction: Let one breath arrive naturally. If breath focus is not supportive, notice one sound instead.

steps.title: Choose one intention
steps.instruction: Complete this sentence: Today, I want to move with a little more… Choose one simple word.

shortVersion.title: Feet and intention
shortVersion.instruction: Feel your feet, allow one natural breath or notice a sound, and choose one word for today.

rituals.closingCheckIn: What would make that intention feel possible rather than demanding?
avoidWhen: Use the sensory alternative if breath attention feels uncomfortable.

rituals.intendedResult: Meet the day with a calm reminder that your attention and pace are yours.

steps.title: Find a gentle edge
steps.instruction: Let your gaze rest on something steady. If imagery helps, imagine a soft, comfortable space around you; otherwise use this only as an intention.

steps.title: Name your pace
steps.instruction: Say quietly: I can meet today at a pace that respects me.

steps.title: Choose one protection
steps.instruction: Choose one small support for your attention: a pause, a shorter reply, a delayed decision, or one moment without input.

shortVersion.title: Choose your pace
shortVersion.instruction: Name one way you will let your pace respect you today.

rituals.closingCheckIn: Which small protection feels easiest to carry into the next hour?
avoidWhen: Choose Feet, Breath, Intention if imagery is not supportive.

rituals.intendedResult: Invite a little more readiness without asking for more energy than you have.

steps.title: Invite warmth
steps.instruction: If it feels comfortable, place your hands near one another or simply notice their temperature. No contact is required.

steps.title: Make a small movement
steps.instruction: Roll or soften your shoulders once. If movement is not right today, notice one place your body is already supported.

steps.title: Choose one next action
steps.instruction: Name the smallest useful next action: water, food, opening a curtain, washing, or sitting up.

shortVersion.title: Small wake-up
shortVersion.instruction: Notice warmth, soften one shoulder, and choose one small next action.

rituals.closingCheckIn: What would be enough energy for the next ten minutes?
avoidWhen: Keep movement optional if your body needs stillness.

rituals.intendedResult: Arrive in the present moment through a light, sensory check-in.

steps.title: Find color and sound
steps.instruction: Notice one color and one sound around you. Neither needs to be pleasant or meaningful.

steps.title: Notice sensation
steps.instruction: Find one neutral sensation: fabric, temperature, a chair, shoes, or air on your skin.

steps.title: Allow one breath
steps.instruction: Let one breath happen naturally, then name one thing that tells you where you are.

shortVersion.title: Arrive through senses
shortVersion.instruction: Notice one color, one sound, one sensation, and one natural breath.

rituals.closingCheckIn: What feels a little more real or available now?
avoidWhen: Skip breath attention and name another neutral sensory detail if needed.

rituals.intendedResult: Keep a discreet point of support during a meeting or interaction.

steps.title: Choose a small anchor
steps.instruction: Notice a small object, a texture in your pocket, fabric at your fingertip, or the edge of a key or bag.

steps.title: Return to texture
steps.instruction: Let your attention return to one detail of that texture whenever you need a quiet point of contact.

steps.title: Keep your place
steps.instruction: Say silently: I can stay here and stay with myself.

shortVersion.title: Quiet anchor
shortVersion.instruction: Notice one small texture and use it as a return point during the interaction.

rituals.closingCheckIn: What object or texture can support you without drawing attention?

rituals.intendedResult: Create one clear boundary before an interaction without needing a long preparation.

steps.title: First natural breath
steps.instruction: Allow one easy breath, or notice one stable object if breath focus is not for you.

steps.title: Second natural breath
steps.instruction: Let your shoulders be as they are. Remember one thing you do not need to explain today.

steps.title: Third breath and boundary
steps.instruction: Allow one more natural breath, then complete: I am available for… and I am not available for…

shortVersion.title: One boundary
shortVersion.instruction: Allow one natural breath or notice one stable object, then name one clear boundary.

rituals.closingCheckIn: What boundary can remain simple and clear?
avoidWhen: Use Pocket Anchor if breath attention is uncomfortable.

rituals.intendedResult: Use optional imagery to sense a flexible, supportive personal boundary.

steps.title: Notice your space
steps.instruction: Notice the space immediately around your body. You do not need to change it.

steps.title: Imagine flexibility, if useful
steps.instruction: If imagery supports you, imagine a boundary that lets care and air move through while keeping your own center intact. You may use this only as an intention.

steps.title: Choose your access
steps.instruction: Name one way you can choose how available you are in the next interaction.

shortVersion.title: Flexible edge
shortVersion.instruction: Imagine or intend a flexible boundary, then choose one way to control your availability.

rituals.closingCheckIn: What does a breathable boundary make possible for you?
avoidWhen: Choose Pocket Anchor if symbolic imagery is not supportive.

rituals.intendedResult: Recognize options and support before entering a demanding environment.

steps.title: Notice stable points
steps.instruction: Find one stable object and one possible exit, doorway, or place to step aside.

steps.title: Choose placement
steps.instruction: Notice where your body would feel most supported: near a wall, closer to an exit, seated, standing, or with more space.

steps.title: Name a break option
steps.instruction: Decide one available option if you need a pause: water, restroom, outside air, a message, or leaving.

shortVersion.title: Find an option
shortVersion.instruction: Notice one stable object, one exit or break option, and one supported place for your body.

rituals.closingCheckIn: Which option helps you remember that you have choices?
avoidWhen: In immediate danger, prioritize moving toward safety and contacting appropriate emergency support.

rituals.intendedResult: Return attention to the present through neutral sensory and physical cues.

steps.title: See and hear
steps.instruction: Name one neutral thing you see and one sound you hear.

steps.title: Feel contact
steps.instruction: Notice one point of body contact and one physical sensation such as temperature, fabric, or air.

steps.title: Name the present
steps.instruction: Say where you are and name one ordinary fact about this moment.

shortVersion.title: Orient
shortVersion.instruction: Name one thing you see, hear, and feel, then name where you are.

rituals.closingCheckIn: Has the present moment become even slightly easier to locate?
avoidWhen: If the environment is unsafe, move toward a safer place first.

rituals.intendedResult: Notice and soften a small amount of physical tension without forcing release.

steps.title: Choose a point of support
steps.instruction: If comfortable, gently press your palms together, press feet into the floor, or press your hands into a soft surface. You can also simply notice support.

steps.title: Pause at the edge
steps.instruction: Notice the feeling of effort for one moment without trying to make it disappear.

steps.title: Release by a degree
steps.instruction: Soften the pressure a little. Let your next movement be smaller rather than bigger.

shortVersion.title: Press and soften
shortVersion.instruction: Notice one point of support, add gentle pressure if comfortable, then soften by a degree.

rituals.closingCheckIn: Where did you notice even a small change in effort?
avoidWhen: Skip physical pressure if contact or movement is not supportive.

rituals.intendedResult: Create one clear attention anchor during racing thoughts or overload.

steps.title: Choose one object
steps.instruction: Find one nearby object that is ordinary and stable.

steps.title: Describe one detail
steps.instruction: Notice its edge, color, weight, shape, or texture without needing to interpret it.

steps.title: Return once
steps.instruction: When your attention runs ahead, return to that one detail one more time.

shortVersion.title: One object
shortVersion.instruction: Choose one ordinary object and describe one detail about it.

rituals.closingCheckIn: What did the object help your attention do?

rituals.intendedResult: Invite a slightly slower pace without controlling or forcing the breath.

steps.title: Notice the breath you have
steps.instruction: Do not change anything at first. Notice the beginning and end of one natural breath.

steps.title: Let the out-breath finish
steps.instruction: If it feels comfortable, let the exhale be just a little less rushed. Do not strain or count.

steps.title: Return to choice
steps.instruction: Notice one place your body is supported, then choose the next small action.

shortVersion.title: Unrush the exhale
shortVersion.instruction: Let one exhale finish without rushing, or notice one point of support instead.

rituals.closingCheckIn: Did anything about the pace of this moment shift?
avoidWhen: Use One-Object Reset if any breath focus feels uncomfortable.

rituals.intendedResult: Reduce unnecessary effort and choose practical support for the capacity you have.

steps.title: Reduce the load
steps.instruction: Name one effort you can make smaller for the next hour.

steps.title: Let one thing wait
steps.instruction: Identify one task, response, or decision that can wait without becoming an emergency.

steps.title: Choose practical support
steps.instruction: Choose one available support: water, food, quiet, a seat, a message for help, or rest.

shortVersion.title: Conserve
shortVersion.instruction: Choose one effort to make smaller and one practical support you can use now.

rituals.closingCheckIn: What have you made a little more manageable?

rituals.intendedResult: Create a short threshold between roles, rooms, calls, tasks, or environments.

steps.title: Mark the ending
steps.instruction: Notice one thing that has just ended: a room, a call, a task, a role, or a conversation.

steps.title: Find the threshold
steps.instruction: Pause at a doorway, a chair, a window, or simply before opening the next screen.

steps.title: Name the next container
steps.instruction: Say: That was then. This is next. Name the one thing you are moving toward.

shortVersion.title: Cross the threshold
shortVersion.instruction: Name what just ended, pause once, and name what comes next.

rituals.closingCheckIn: What can you leave with the last role or task?

rituals.intendedResult: Mark the end of the day with optional movement, reflection, and symbolic release.

steps.title: Change one detail
steps.instruction: If it feels useful, change one environmental detail: dim a light, wash your hands, change rooms, or place your phone face down.

steps.title: Name what can wait
steps.instruction: Choose one feeling, task, or conversation that can wait until another time.

steps.title: Release in your own way
steps.instruction: Move, stretch, imagine setting something down, or simply say: This day can be complete enough.

shortVersion.title: Mark the end
shortVersion.instruction: Change one small detail and name one thing that can wait until tomorrow.

rituals.closingCheckIn: What would help this day feel complete enough?
avoidWhen: Keep movement and imagery optional if they are not supportive.

rituals.intendedResult: Create a more intentional relationship with visual input, body effort, and notifications.

steps.title: Create visual distance
steps.instruction: Move your gaze away from the screen for one moment and look at a farther point or neutral surface.

steps.title: Release one effort
steps.instruction: Soften your jaw, hands, shoulders, or posture by a small degree. Movement is optional.

steps.title: Choose one notification boundary
steps.instruction: Choose one action: mute, close, delay, reduce tabs, change brightness, or set the device down briefly.

shortVersion.title: Step back from the screen
shortVersion.instruction: Look away once, soften one effort, and choose one notification boundary.

rituals.closingCheckIn: What would make your next screen moment feel more chosen?

rituals.intendedResult: Separate your own experience from what may belong to another person or situation.

steps.title: Name what is present
steps.instruction: Name one feeling, request, pressure, or situation that is taking up space.

steps.title: Ask the boundary question
steps.instruction: Ask: Is this mine to carry, mine to respond to, both, or neither?

steps.title: Choose one honest action
steps.instruction: Choose a small action that matches your answer: pause, ask, decline, offer less, or return to your own need.

shortVersion.title: Ask what is yours
shortVersion.instruction: Ask what is yours to carry or respond to, then choose one action that matches.

rituals.closingCheckIn: What became clearer when you separated the question?

rituals.intendedResult: Build a repeatable personal cue that helps you return to steadiness across days.

steps.title: Choose one cue
steps.instruction: Choose one calming texture, scent, sound, or object that is available to you. It can be very ordinary.

steps.title: Notice one detail
steps.instruction: Stay with one detail of the cue for a few moments: temperature, shape, sound, texture, or familiarity.

steps.title: Make it repeatable
steps.instruction: Decide where or when you could return to this same cue again: at your desk, by the door, in a bag, or before rest.

shortVersion.title: Return to one cue
shortVersion.instruction: Choose one familiar sensory cue and decide when you will return to it again.

rituals.closingCheckIn: Which cue would you like to become a reliable home base?
